what_it_does: When a processor executes instructions out of order to stay busy, it must figure out whether a load (reading from memory) might depend on an earlier store (write to memory) that has not yet resolved its address. This is called memory dependence prediction. A related but opposite trick — speculative memory bypassing — lets a load get its value directly from a store without waiting, skipping the usual address-match check. The trouble is these two tasks need opposite error tolerances: the first must never miss a real dependence, while the second must never falsely claim independence. Mascot is a single predictor structure (inspired by TAGE, a well-known branch-history prediction design that uses multiple tables keyed on increasingly long history patterns) that learns both when two instructions definitely conflict and when they definitely do not, letting one hardware block serve both use cases.
